title: Bounded etale tensor origin for an open-supported finite-Tor complex
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a map $A	o B$ of finite commutative unital rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$, schemes $U,Z$, and an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites, with exact site comparison $
u_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and open extensions $j_!^{\mathrm{et},A}$ and $j_!^{\mathrm{pro},A}$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $M$ have bounded intrinsically constructible pro-etale cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Write $M_B=T_U^{A,B}M$ for scalar extension [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. There exists a bounded etale $A$-complex $L$ with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] and $
u_U^*L\simeq M$. Put $K=j_!^{\mathrm{et},A}L$, $N=j_!^{\mathrm{pro},A}M$, and $H=K\otimes^L_{A_{Z,\mathrm{et}}}B_{Z,\mathrm{et}}$, regarding $B$ as an $A$-module [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Then $K$ and $H$ are bounded etale $A$-complexes, and there are canonical identifications, relative to $
u_U^*L\simeq M$,
$$
u_Z^*K\simeq N,\qquad

u_Z^*H\simeq N\otimes^L_{A_Z}B_Z\simeq\operatorname{Res}_{A	o B}j_!^{\mathrm{pro},B}M_B.$$
In particular both $K$ and $H$ lie in $D^+$, without assuming $B$ has finite Tor dimension over $A$.

proof.text: For every integer q apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-sheaf-origin] to the intrinsically constructible A-module sheaf H^q(M). It gives a globally constructible etale A-module sheaf F_q with nu_U^*F_q isomorphic to H^q(M). The ring A is finite and U is an arbitrary scheme, precisely the hypotheses of that node; no Noetherianity of U is used. Since M is bounded, [lem-weil-pbc-fixed-module-bounded-constructible-origin] now gives a bounded etale complex L with globally constructible cohomology and an isomorphism e:nu_U^*L -> M. Fix this witness e for the remaining canonical identifications.

source.place: Tags 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible) and 09AL (lemma-compare-constructible-derived); finite-ring global-stratification versions recorded in the cited nodes

proof.text: Set K=j_!^{et,A}L and N=j_!^{pro,A}M. Etale extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]; pro-etale extension by zero is exact and acts degreewise by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives H^q(K)=j_!^{et,A}H^q(L) and H^q(N)=j_!^{pro,A}H^q(M); in particular both are bounded. Apply [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] degreewise to a representative of L. Its natural sheaf isomorphism is a chain isomorphism, and the exact functors on both sides preserve quasi-isomorphisms, so it gives nu_Z^*K isomorphic to j_!^{pro,A}nu_U^*L. Composing with j_!^{pro,A}(e) gives the required canonical identification nu_Z^*K isomorphic to N.

source.place: Tag 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison); exactness from sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), cohomology from homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor)

proof.text: Regard the degree-zero constant sheaf B_{Z,et} as an A_{Z,et}-module and put H=K tensor^L_A B_{Z,et}. The constant-ring identification in [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], applied to A and B, identifies nu_Z^*B_{Z,et} with B_Z, including its A-action: the identifications preserve constant sections and therefore the structural map A -> B. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the comparison morphism with the structural ring isomorphism nu_Z^{-1}A_{Z,et} -> A_Z. Its derived pullback is termwise nu_Z^*, since that functor is exact. It gives nu_Z^*H isomorphic to (nu_Z^*K) tensor^L_{A_Z} B_Z, hence to N tensor^L_{A_Z}B_Z by Step 2. This use of the tensor comparison is in the unbounded derived categories; no boundedness of H has yet been asserted.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); constant-coefficient exactness as recorded in lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact

proof.text: Choose integers a <= b witnessing the finite Tor amplitude of M. By [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], testing this very interval against the degree-zero A_U-module B_U gives H^q(Q)=0 for q outside [a,b], where Q=M tensor^L_{A_U}B_U is viewed as an A-complex. This tests M against B_U and imposes no flatness or projective-dimension condition on B.

Apply [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] with coefficient ring A, complex M on U and degree-zero complex B_Z on Z. Restriction of B_Z is canonically B_U by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], so N tensor^L_{A_Z}B_Z is canonically j_!^{pro,A}Q. The scalar extension M_B of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](1) is computed by P tensor_A B_U for a K-flat representative P of M, with B_U acting on the right factor. Forgetting this B-action leaves exactly the complex computing Q. Thus Q is canonically Res_{A->B}M_B, with the identification induced by the identity on that tensor complex. The restriction-of-scalars compatibility in [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] gives j_!^{pro,A}Q isomorphic to Res_{A->B}j_!^{pro,B}M_B. This proves the second claimed identification. Exactness of that same j_! and the cohomology formula of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] show that j_!^{pro,A}Q, and consequently nu_Z^*H by Step 3, have cohomology only in [a,b].

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); the scalar extension is the K-flat construction in Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change)

proof.text: For q outside [a,b], exactness and the cohomology comparison of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] identify nu_Z^*H^q(H) with H^q(nu_Z^*H)=0 by Step 5. By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], nu_Z^* is faithful on A-module sheaves. Therefore nu_Z^*(id_{H^q(H)})=0 implies id_{H^q(H)}=0, so H^q(H)=0. Thus H is bounded in [a,b]. Together with Step 2, K and H are bounded etale A-complexes and in particular belong to D^+. All identifications were the canonical comparisons followed by the fixed origin witness e; no further choices of isomorphisms were made.

split_report.summary: Constructible sheaf comparison and the existing bounded derived-origin node provide L without a Noetherian hypothesis. Exact open extension gives K and its pro-etale comparison. The unbounded tensor comparison and open projection identify nu*H with j_!(M tensor_A^L B); the Tor interval of M bounds this object, and exact faithful comparison reflects that interval to H. All proof ingredients already have DAG nodes; no new node and no statement change.

Step 1: Stacks 09AK holds for an arbitrary scheme, and the sheaf-origin node plus the fixed-module bounded-origin node give a bounded constructible L with nu*L≅M. Step 2: étale and pro-étale j_! are exact, and the 09AF comparison is natural, so it gives a chain isomorphism termwise; nu*K≅N. Step 3: nu*B_et=B_proet as an A-module; the ringed-topoi tensor pullback (07A4) holds unbounded, with Lu*=termwise nu* because nu* is exact. Step 4: the 08FZ definition tests every module sheaf, so B_U is a valid test; no flatness of B is needed. Step 5: projection formula (0GL1), then j^{-1}B_Z=B_U (constant-ring-map node), then Q=Res M_B by the K-flat model of det-sp-scalar-extension-functor(1), then the Res/j_! clause of lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero; exactness keeps the bound [a,b]. Step 6: nu* is exact and fully faithful on module sheaves (099T), so it reflects zero cohomology and H is bounded. This matches parent det-sp-reduction-direct-image Steps 1 and 3 (D^+ inputs) and blueprint main-20261015 sk-lem-sp-reduction-direct-image Step 1. Edge cases checked: U=∅, B=0, A=B, and Z/ℓ²→F_ℓ (M=A gives bounded Q; M=F_ℓ is excluded by finite Tor). No duplicate of the whole item in the DAG. The declared tool_uses (pbc origin, cbc j_!, sf comparison, ringed-topoi tensor, constant ring map, pe classical) are generic tools and I accept them. Advisory: lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin alone would give Step 1 and the interval reflection.
